At first/last index, arg!=0 returns; arg0 consults descriptor.byte3 and returns if0. Color row72 byte3=1 admits circular movement at edges.
Wrappers call list_step(L,delta -1 or +1,transition_flag1). Scan counts entries with item.byte178!=0 and searches both sides of current index; +8a and +17a are separate bytes.

Eligible changed target: old item vslot70 if not default52c0d6c4, then STRH new index to L+1ce, then new item vslot6c if L.byte1d0!=0 and not default52c0d6c0; optional focus-change function if L.byte224!=0. Exact actual color-row dynamic vptr not recovered.

Wrapping scan clears transition flag. Immediate path calls focus_set and scroll_set. Nonwrap requested transition enters52c0e838, sets L.byte1dc=2, calls actual focus_set before scheduler registration528f8228. No animation ticks or displayed frames tested.

A direction event reaching list_step at 0x52c0e948 invokes stop-transition first. State2 requests scheduler removal, applies saved scroll target and re-enters focus_set with current focus, then clears state1dc and field20c. The second events in e0->e4 and df->e3 return at 0x5278daa0 and 0x5278d9dc before list_step, retaining focus and state2 without a removal request. State1 is outside the replay.

Item base constructor initializes178=1,179=1,17a=0. Generic visibility setter writes8a. The color confirm path checks17a. Synthetic retained-row flags test does not prove real hidden-row membership/count or actual178 writer policy.
First registration block installs copied menu-pointer closure in L+214, manager5278b7b0 at+21c, invoker5278ecd0 at+220, enables+224. Source literal instructions, not a fixed ROM vtable slot.

L+220 invoked with closure L+214,new focus.5278ecd0 dereferences captured menu then calls5278ec04. Color descriptor+38/+3c=0 skips row-specific hook; byte0=1 reaches presentation update5278e4ac. This is independent from option confirmation/store.

limitations: No physical button, dial or touch identity assigned to event values. Upstream hardware/input producer is not traced.

No full window lifecycle, actual display output, persistence, peripheral IO or firmware change. Synthetic valid objects/geometry are supplied; constructor/visibility policy that maintains real list membership is not executed.

50 public replay cases: menu direction 8, four-row traversal 16, eligibility 12, retained-row flags 4, focus setter 5, pending-state2 cleanup 1 and edge retention 2, first registration fragment to real menu callback 2. Prior population/confirm cases are separate.

Direction wrappers and full list/focus/geometry/transition functions execute original ARM on selected branches. Full source ranges include untested branches, especially motion state1, zero-sized lists and all-ineligible lists.

Item+178 is navigation eligibility in this bounded consumer. Its relation to a real hidden/disabled-row producer is not proven. Synthetic+8a=0 or+17a=1 with the item retained tests field independence only.
Item vslots6c/70 are exercised with supplied callbacks, or with proven base no-op functions. No actual color-screen derived item vtable target is claimed. Boundaries are not physical drawing.

Two callback-install cases execute5278dcd0..5278dd54 only, then full installer and closure manager; other two action registrations are not executed. Real5278ecd0/5278ec04 run afterward;5278e4ac is explicitly stubbed as presentation boundary.
Scheduler add/remove, clock, render invalidation, synthetic heap/free, assertions and supplied callback targets are explicitly listed stubs. No asynchronous animation tick is delivered.

Genuine angr C is retained unedited and can misrepresent predicated instructions/types; ARM and scoped execution are authoritative. Offsets are hexadecimal unless descriptor index72 is explicitly decimal.
